visible_difference: This is a real change of mechanism. The pause now comes from boundary punctuation in the fenced spoken text, not from performance notes in the preamble. The n4a|n4b join becomes a sentence boundary, and full stops are the one boundary the reader was measured to honor every time: minimum 0.40 s in take 1 and 0.68 s in take 2, across 21 sentence joins. The full stop also agrees with the fixed preamble ('A normal breath at a full stop is right') rather than fighting it. The n3a|n3b join gets a comma, the only legal mark there. A comma was honored in 1 of 2 observed takes. The take-3 explicit-silence wording, which ran to 68.5 s, is removed by restoring the take-1 direction, so the new take tests punctuation alone. The plan's expected result now says honestly that line 3 is uncertain, and it names the next mechanism if line 3 fails: merge n3a and n3b, or change the preamble in tooling.

house_rule_check: Both edits comply. Line 3, 'Clinicians sign in with their usual credentials, and ask in plain language.', has a single comma BEFORE the conjunction, not after it. It is not one of a pair of commas fencing a hedge. Line 4, 'The answers carry citations. To medical literature and clinical guidelines.', adds only a full stop and a capital T. Neither line adds a colon, a semicolon or a dash. No sentence opens with And or But, and there is no first person. The fragment is acceptable in captions under the house rules. No rule bans a fragment. Read with the cue before it ('The answers carry citations.'), it is unambiguous, and it is ordinary broadcast style. It is also better than the earlier comma, which split a noun from its complement. No spoken word changes, because the soundcheck's normalise() and narration_tokens both lowercase and drop punctuation, so 'To' is the same token as 'to'. Token count and word_range are unchanged (n4a 41 to 45, n4b 45 to 51). No claim id, clause id, vo_claims entry or claims.json byte changes. The capital 'To' and the full stop matter only where a check compares exact strings. In the code I read, the punctuation-sensitive comparisons are the three copies the director named: scenes[].vo against vo_script.txt, the vo_direction line 'text' against the script, and opening-a.json as a byte copy of storyboard.json. creative_direction.edits[].sentence_to_shot.clause for s3 and s4 is a verbatim copy too, so update it to match exactly, as planned. Three other places carry the old punctuation but are compared only as tokens, so leaving them breaks nothing: narration_picture.clauses n3a, n4a and n4b text, and the authored captions c5, c7 and c8 (provisional; board_retime replaces them with measured cues).
